correctness.rationale: From the two prefix-sum inequalities and nonnegativity one derives all vertices 0, A_i=pe_i, B_j=(p+q)e_(p+j), C_ij=pe_i+qe_(p+j). For a two-block symmetric center, the four exact squared-distance forms and F=(q-2)(p+q)^2-qp^2, K=p²+3pq+q² show B_j always on the proposed sphere; A_i exactly when F<0; mixed vertices never; origin only for p=q=1. The proposed center is a convex combination of its contacting vertices, giving global minimality and uniqueness by weighted variance identity. Since q(q-2)=(q-1)^2-1 is not square when q>=3, no integer F=0 case. Independently verified 576 rational p,q distance/contact comparisons including the boundary. This proof, not the test grid, covers all positive integer p,q.

originality.rationale: Athanasiadis defines these exact composition polytopes and proves lattice counting/gamma-positivity, while Chapoton and Pitman–Stanley give more general combinatorial constructions. Those results do not compute Euclidean minimal enclosing balls under the canonical coordinate metric. A same-day octopus arbor-polytope circumball classification was read in full, but its inequalities cap individual first-block coordinates, yielding a different Euclidean vertex set; its three-phase result does not imply the present exact F-dependent contact collapse. No stronger same-object metric theorem was found in targeted primary and Resultary comparisons; historical priority remains qualified.
